targets.summary: The wrapper should not run gcx with `go run ...@latest`, which requires Go. Users should install the gcx binary from the curl install link instead.
targets.adoption_evidence: Before: `GCX_CMD=(go run "${GCX_MODULE:-github.com/grafana/gcx/cmd/gcx@latest}")`, which needed Go (`if ! command -v go ...; echo "error: go is needed to run gcx."`). In the merged version that line is gone, along with the Go check. The script now uses gcx's curl install script: `curl -fsSL "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/grafana/gcx/v${GCX_VERSION}/scripts/install.sh" | INSTALL_DIR="${tmp}" VERSION="${GCX_VERSION}" sh` (inside `_ensure_gcx`), and `_run_gcx` calls the prebuilt binary with `"${GCX_BIN}" "$@"`. The user doesn't run the installer by hand, because the wrapper does it automatically. Still, the result matches the request: Go is no longer needed, and gcx comes from the curl install link.
targets.stage3_reason: `GCX_CMD=(go run "...gcx/cmd/gcx@latest")` makes every user install a Go toolchain and runs an unpinned `@latest` build from source, which is a real design and supply-chain problem that a reviewer can see in the code. The merged code drops Go and instead caches a pinned prebuilt binary through gcx's curl installer (`curl -fsSL "${installer}" | ... VERSION="${GCX_VERSION}" sh`), as the maintainer asked.
